sentences.text: Veillonella are anaerobic, non-motile, small spherical Gram-negative cocci that do not ferment glucose or other carbohydrates.
They grow on organic acids, producing propionic and acetic acids, carbon dioxide and hydrogen from lactate, and consume lactic acid in oral biofilms.
In the mouth they are early colonisers of dental plaque and partner metabolically with streptococci, whose lactic acid serves as their carbon source.
Veillonella also occur in the human small intestine and, with Prevotella, among the predominant commensal genera of healthy lungs, which often harbour organisms from the mouth.
Studies have reported Veillonella parvula increasing in the intestine in inflammatory bowel disease and enrichment of lower airways with this species in lung cancer progression.
